events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: As part of Native American Heritage Month , join us for an evening conversation with James Johnson. James will discuss his artistic practice, the importance of preserving traditional Tlingit ways of creating, and how he draws on the knowledge and work of his ancestors in his contemporary practice. James Johnson is an award-winning Tlingit Artist and Carver, born and raised in Juneau, AK. He belongs to the Tlingit Ch’áak’ Dakl’aweidi Clan (Eagle Killerwhale). James is a multi-disciplinary artist but specializes in Tlingit formline design, with a focus on traditional wood carving. Carving is an integral part of the preservation of Tlingit history and culture. “Carving is our visual language that represents who the Tlingit people are, and how we live in balance with all things.” James’s contemporary practice builds upon an indigenous artistic continuum while honoring the culture and its rich traditions. This event takes place on a Legendary Late Hours day and is included with admission. The event takes place in the Montgomery Ward Lecture Hall, on the lower level.

The Black Hawk Performance Company seeks to honor the ground we dance on, Mother Earth and the many tribes who have made Illinois their home. Many tribes like the Ojibwe, Odawa and Potawatomi and numerous others  have been here for thousands of years and are still here now. Most American Indian people, 70%, live in urban areas like Chicago now. The most famous American Indian leader of historic times was the great Sauk Chief Black Hawk. events.display_title: Exploring Indigenous Ingenuity in Ancient Americas
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Join the Field Museum for Exploring Indigenous Ingenuity in Ancient Americas , a professional development workshop presented in celebration of Native American Heritage Month . Educators will investigate how Indigenous peoples across the Americas developed scientific knowledge and technological innovations through close observation, experimentation, creativity, and relationships with the land. Participants will engage in inquiry-based, hands-on activities that explore Indigenous ingenuity through a STEAM lens . The workshop will connect ancestral innovations to living Indigenous communities, contemporary knowledge, and cultural identity. Open to formal and informal STEAM educators of all grade levels . Illinois educators will earn 3 Professional Development hours . Registration includes workshop materials and museum admission.

events.title: Celebrate Diwali at the Field Museum!
events.display_title: [FREE] Celebrate Diwali at the Field Museum!
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Join us for our second annual Diwali celebration as we honor the Festival of Lights and the rich cultural traditions of South Asia! Experience an afternoon of vibrant dance performances, interactive cultural activities, and opportunities to explore the connections between science, history, and tradition. From classical Indian dance and contemporary Bollywood to an engaging conversation on Ayurveda, discover how South Asian traditions celebrate light, knowledge, and renewal. Music will be provided by DJ J-Mean. Our popular henna station returns this year, free for all attendees! Guests can also connect with local community organizations and learn more about the diverse cultures, traditions, and contributions of South Asian communities throughout Chicagoland. Featured Dance Performances The following take place in Stanley Field Hall Mandala Arts | Bharatanatyam Experience the beauty and storytelling of Bharatanatyam, a classical Indian dance tradition rooted in South India. Through intricate movements, expressive gestures, and rhythmic footwork, Mandala Arts brings to life stories and traditions that have been shared across generations. U Chicago Raas | Raas-Garba Celebrate the energy and joy of Raas-Garba, traditional folk dances from Gujarat, India. U Chicago Raas brings a contemporary collegiate interpretation of these vibrant traditions, combining rhythmic movement, colorful choreography, and the spirit of community celebration. Latin School of Chicago - Latin Laddoos Performance Group The South Asian Students of the Latin School (Junior K to 8th Grade) will perform contemporary and traditional group dance. They have performed dances choreographed by Bollywood Groove and Meher Dance in 2026. Rhythm Roots | Bollywood and Indian Folk Dance Get ready for a lively celebration of Indian dance! Featuring talented young performers ages 6–14, Rhythm Roots showcases an exciting blend of Bollywood, Garba, Bhangra, and contemporary fusion. Guests will also have an opportunity to join the fun through an interactive dance experience!

events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Come join Fabiani Herrera, Negaunee Associate Curator of Paleobotany, as he reveals the mysteries behind 120-million-year-old fossilized plants from Mongolia through the use of a Scanning Electron Microscope. Examine different parts of these fossil plants under the Scanning Electron Microscope and Wentzscope to reveal the tiny secrets that shaped the Age of Dinosaurs and beyond! Discover the characteristics of these ancient plants that connect them to some of their modern relatives and help scientists map their evolutionary lineage.
